verses.text: Trouble for you who wrecked other people without getting wrecked, who betrayed people without getting betrayed! When you're done destroying, you'll be destroyed. When you're done betraying, you'll be betrayed.
LORD, show us grace. We've been waiting for you. Be our strength every morning and save us when trouble comes.
At the roar of thunder, the peoples run. When you rise up, the nations scatter.
What you took will be gathered up the way caterpillars gather. People will jump on it like locusts.
The LORD is lifted high because he lives up high. He's filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Your times will have a solid footing, with plenty of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Your treasure is standing in awe of the LORD.
Look, their bravest men are crying outside. The messengers sent to make peace are weeping hard.
The highways are empty. Travelers have stopped coming. He's broken the agreement, treated cities with contempt, and shown no respect for anybody.
The land mourns and wastes away. Lebanon is humiliated and drying up. Sharon looks like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel have been stripped bare.
“Now I'll get up,” says the LORD. “Now I'll rise high. Now I'll be lifted up.
You'll get pregnant with husks and give birth to stubble. Your own breath is the fire that'll eat you up.
The peoples will burn like stone in a lime kiln, like thorns cut down and tossed in the fire.
You who are far away, hear what I've done. You who are close, recognize my strength.”
Sinners in Zion are terrified. The godless can't stop shaking. “Who among us can live with a fire that eats everything up? Who can live with flames that never go out?”
The person who does what's right and speaks honestly, who wants no profit from oppressing people, waves away a bribe, blocks their ears to talk of bloodshed, and shuts their eyes to evil,
will live up high with a fortress of rock to defend them. They'll have bread to eat and water they can count on.
You'll see the king in all his beauty with your own eyes. You'll see a land stretching far away.
You'll think back on the terror. Where's the one who counted? Where's the one who weighed everything? Where's the one who counted the towers?
You won't see those fierce people again, the people whose speech is too hard to follow, whose strange language you can't understand.
Look at Zion, the city where we keep our appointed feasts. You'll see Jerusalem, a peaceful home, a tent that won't be moved. Its stakes will never be pulled out, and none of its ropes will snap.
There the LORD will be with us in his majesty, like a place with wide rivers and streams where no warship with oars and no grand ship will pass.
The LORD is our judge. The LORD gives us our laws. The LORD is our king. He'll save us.
Your ropes hang loose. Nobody could hold the mast steady at its base or spread the sail. Then all that plunder was divided up. Even people who couldn't walk well got a share.
Nobody who lives there will say, “I'm sick.” The people there will be forgiven for what they've done wrong.
